source: NCERT Class VII, Our Pasts II, History Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Why Rulers Built
points: Rulers built **temples, mosques, tanks, wells, forts, palaces and tombs** — to show **power, piety and generosity**.
Temples/mosques were meant to be **models of the world** (the cosmos) and displayed the ruler's devotion.
Building **reservoirs and tanks** (e.g. Sultan Iltutmish's **Hauz-i-Sultani**) won praise for the ruler.

sub: Roofs, doors and windows made by placing a **horizontal beam across two vertical columns**.
Used in temples, mosques, tanks and palaces of the period.
Weight of the roof carried by **arches**; the **'true' arch** and the **dome** appeared.
Two new materials helped: high-quality **limestone cement** (mortar) and **superior mortar** made construction of arches/domes possible.

sections.heading: 3. Temple Architecture
points: The **Kandariya Mahadeva temple (999 CE, Khajuraho)** — built by the **Chandela** king Dhangadeva; dedicated to **Shiva**.
The **Rajarajeshvara (Brihadeshwara) temple, Thanjavur** — built by **Rajaraja I** (Chola), with the tallest **shikhara** of its time.

Temple parts: **garbhagriha** (shrine of the main deity), **shikhara/vimana** (tower), **mandapa** (hall); temples were also centres of **power, wealth and devotion** — hence often **targeted in wars**.

sections.heading: 4. Sultanate and Mughal Buildings
points: **Qutb Minar** (begun by Qutbuddin Aibak, completed by Iltutmish) and the **Alai Darwaza** (Alauddin Khalji, a **true dome and arch**).
Mughal gardens laid out as **chahar bagh** — a **four-quartered** garden divided by water channels/walkways (e.g. at **Kashmir, Agra, Delhi**).
**Humayun's Tomb**, the **Taj Mahal** (Shah Jahan, for Mumtaz Mahal), and the **Red Fort** — grand domes, arches and **pietra dura** (inlay of coloured stones).
Shah Jahan's audience hall linked kingship with **divine justice**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Trabeate = beam on two columns (pre-1200); Arcuate = arch & dome (post-1200) using limestone cement.
Kandariya Mahadeva temple = Khajuraho (Chandelas, Shiva, 999 CE).
Qutb Minar = Aibak→Iltutmish; Alai Darwaza (true dome/arch) = Alauddin Khalji.
Mughal garden = chahar bagh (four-part); Taj Mahal = Shah Jahan; pietra dura = stone inlay.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **'true' arch and dome** became common **after c. 1200** with limestone cement/mortar.
